newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors to shift back to stocks, bonds - poll.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors to shift back to stocks, bonds - poll.

text.p: Japan-based institutional investors are planning to increase their investments in stocks and bonds in September while slashing their cash holdings, a Reuters investment survey showed on Friday.

It showed that fading expectations of a credit tightening in both the United States and Japan had led to the change, and a decision by U.S. authorities earlier in August to keep rates steady, in particular, was behind the increase in bond investments.
The average weighting for cash instruments fell by more than a full percentage point to its lowest level since January this year, the monthly Global Asset Allocation survey showed.
It asked 17 Japan-based financial institutions about their recommended investment strategy in September.

In stock investments, weightings of British and German shares were lifted considerably. Investors said favourable corporate results in both nations coupled with the low interest rate policy throughout Europe were behind the moves.
In contrast, investors shunned the French equity market due to concerns over the franc, seen vulnerable to possible turmoil over the plans for a single European currency.
Weightings of North American stocks, though lowered slightly, remained at high levels.
Many investors said they believed the recent downward correction which hit Wall Street had already come to a halt.

They also see any U.S. credit tightening as having been put on hold for the time being. "It will be put off until the (November) presidential elections are over," said an analyst at Nikko Research Center.
Investors kept their weightings of Japanese stocks at high levels, although many expect them to go through a downward correction in the near term.

Fears of an oversupply arising from the expected release of new stocks by Japanese banks and West Japan Railway Co, as well as concerns over the outlook of the economy were likely to push down share prices.

Approaching half-year corporate book closings at the end of September also posed a risk for the Tokyo stock market. Sales aimed at window-dressing corporate results and poor results themselves may drag down share prices, investors said.
"Shares may ease temporarily, but that would be an excellent chance to buy on dips," said an analyst at Tokyo Research Institute Inc.
Weightings of Asian stocks were lowered, but many investors said their long-term strategy was to increase their investments.
In bond investments, weightings of Japanese, U.S. and Canadian markets were raised. The weightings for Canada stood at their highest level since the survey began in March 1995.
"It should be noted that coupons of U.S., Canadian and Australian bonds are relatively high and have little risk of capital losses," said Nomura Research Institute.

High weightings for Australian bonds lifted the weightings for the Asian market as a whole, although some investors said they would turn cautious towards Australia due to a risk that its currency may take an unexpected dip.
Although investors plan to increase their Japanese bond investments, they would not be able to make aggressive moves as chances of a credit tightening still remained, they said.
On the European front, investors lowered most of their weightings except for British and German bonds.
Uncertainty over the plans for a single European currency and views that rates in Germany may have already hit bottom were making investors cautious, they said.
